# Cover image decoders

These limits apply to book covers and the bounded legacy small-JPEG wallpaper compatibility path, not the new streaming wallpaper decoder. Wallpaper PNG uses a separately namespaced instance of the same pngle/miniz sources, including a zero-input drain when the inflater retains output after consuming the final IDAT input. Large JPEG wallpapers use the separately pinned [TJpgDec core](<tjpgd/README.md>). See [0.8.31 wallpaper notes](<../../../docs/0.8.31大图壁纸.md>) for the independent input, pixel and memory limits.

- `stb_image.h`: nothings/stb, commit `003501f6d7a8668ce8b6d875e34dd97ad0d5d5b5`, v2.30. Only JPEG is enabled. Folio changes corrupt post-SOF marker handling from partial success to failure and accepts missing restart markers only after the final MCU of a scan. An optional `STBI_JPEG_CANCELLED` hook stops baseline/progressive entropy decoding at each MCU/block row through the normal error cleanup path. Dual MIT / Public Domain license is retained at the end and in `stb_image.LICENSE`.
- `pngle/`: kikuchan/pngle, commit `b1c68193f1d3f8642b3e0e095d457a828038e6fb`, MIT. Its bundled miniz v1.15 is Public Domain; both notices and complete texts are retained. Original source URLs and SHA-256 values are recorded in `cover-origins.json`.

Folio's source edits to pngle add an optional `PNGLE_OUTPUT_CHECK` hook at the start of `pngle_on_data`, rejecting output beyond the prevalidated non-interlaced IHDR size; an inflater-status hook requires the zlib stream to finish before accepting IEND; and unsigned casts in `read_uint32` avoid signed left-shift overflow on chunk lengths/CRCs. The embedding translation unit redirects allocations to a bounded PSRAM-first allocator, disables gamma conversion, and prefixes miniz symbols so the decoder cannot replace ESP32 ROM miniz symbols used by EPUB ZIP parsing. Neither vendor is compiled as a separate translation unit.

Folio accepts non-interlaced 8-bit PNG (gray, gray/alpha, RGB, RGBA or palette) and JPEG supported by stb. PNG is decoded by scanline into a 192 × 288 maximum area-averaged thumbnail, so its source-size RGBA frame is never allocated. JPEG uses grayscale output. Inputs are limited to 2 MiB, 2,000,000 pixels and 4096 pixels per dimension. Decoder allocations have a 4 MiB live budget; input bytes and up to eight cached thumbnails are additional. Allocation failure falls back to text. No fonts or third-party cover artwork are bundled with these decoders.
